Thanks for taking this RFP. Attached is the latest version of our data residency questionnaire (procureit_questionnaire_v3.pdf). There are a few follow-up items we need clarified before procurement can move to legal: in particular, we need the exact activation criteria for a warm-standby region, how data routing is controlled during failover, and what evidence you can provide for data-at-rest residency in the EU across the different deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private).

We'd appreciate a written response and a short call to walk through the answers. Target procurement deadline: July 2.

Mina — notes below, feel free to trim for external. I'll keep this technical.

1) Warm-standby activation criteria (deterministic):
- Primary region health checks: sustained instance-level errors > 5% of requests over a 3-minute sliding window, OR error budget burn > 60% within 5 minutes.
- Resource saturation: compute queue latency > configured threshold (default 300ms P99) AND autoscale unable to provision additional capacity for 2 contiguous minutes.
- Network partition: loss of control-plane connectivity to the primary region nodes for 30s with no successful retries.
- Manual/operational activation: CS/ops can force activation via console with documented approval flow.

Activation workflow: once a trigger is met, smart-routing flips to a pre-warmed pool in the standby region. We keep a KV-cache checkpoint and prefix-caching window to reduce cold-start regressions. TTL for automatic rollback is configurable (default 30 min), but ops will monitor and manually confirm resume.

2) Data traversal and residency during activation:
- We design the warm-standby so that serving can occur from the standby region without persistent writes to non-EU object stores. Temporary ephemeral caches (in-memory or ephemeral SSD) may be used in the standby region.
- Cross-region control-plane chatter (telemetry/heartbeat) may touch non-EU telemetry collectors if customer has opted into global telemetry — we can disable global telemetry per-account.
- Persistent storage for EU-bound customers is pinned to EU object stores unless they are on a Dedicated pool explicitly configured to span regions (rare; requires customer opt-in).
- For Hosted customers: in the default profile, we will not write primary customer data to non-EU stores. For Dedicated: configuration can lock physical storage to EU-only nodes. For Private: customer manages storage locality on-prem/VPC.

3) Evidence & auditability:
- We can provide: signed region-attestation (pdf), time-stamped access logs showing serving node IPs and ASNs, object-store bucket write/read receipts (with timestamps), and a config snapshot showing region pinning settings.
- Logs: per-request trace IDs that map to node IDs and region. Retention is configurable; a 12-month export is standard for enterprise.

Attachments proposal for response package:
- redwood_locale_response.pdf (formal QA summary + short diagrams)
- residency_matrix.xlsx (table mapping deployment mode -> storage locus -> failover behaviour)

Caveats: if a customer requires cryptographic-hardware-backed locking (HSM key in-EU), that is supported via KMS integration but requires provisioning lead time.

Ben
Senior Product Manager, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Anna / EuroFin procurement team —

Thanks for the questions. Attached is a concise response pack (redwood_locale_response.pdf) and a residency_matrix spreadsheet that maps each deployment mode to the storage locus, failover behaviour, and available evidence artifacts. Summary below (pasteable bullets for procurement/legal):

- Activation criteria: automatic warm-standby activation is deterministic and based on health/error budget thresholds, autoscale failures, or control-plane partitioning; there is also a documented manual activation path. (See page 2 of response pack.)
- Data traversal: under our default Hosted profile for EU customers, we do not persist customer data outside EU object stores. Ephemeral caches in a warm-standby region may be used for in-flight serving; these caches are transient and not configured for long-term persistence. Cross-region telemetry can be disabled for EU accounts.
- Evidence: we provide a signed region attestation, time-stamped per-request logs mapping to serving node IDs and region, S3-compatible bucket access receipts, and a config snapshot evidencing region pinning. Standard log retention: 12 months; longer retention available under enterprise add-on.
- Dedicated & Private: Dedicated capacity can be configured to pin both serving and storage to EU-only racks (requires contractual configuration). Private deployments are fully customer-managed and can be air-gapped; we will provide the same evidence package via the customer's audit process.

Attachments included: redwood_locale_response.pdf, residency_matrix.xlsx (both attached).

Next step: suggest a 30-min call to review any contractual language and confirm the DocuSign template. I’m available Thu 25th 09:00-11:00 or Fri 26th 14:00-16:00 CEST.

Regards,
